evidence.title: Every run_once performs two complete archive parses despite 100000-row memory window; historical replay can expand archive and worsen the scan cost
evidence.proof_level: Fresh exact-SHA source-path audit and algorithmic bound; NOT benchmark, exact-repository pytest, full-production run_once reproduction, or confirmed production incident
exact_chain: contracts.py:219-234 observation_id hashes economic identity/value/clocks/revision but omits provenance, data_quality and quality_flags.
providers.py JsonlFlowAdapter.collect parses external JSONL rows; runner.py:110-118 records successful parse as collector OK before archive append.

storage.py:49-91 append_observations calls load_observations(max_records=100000) at line 64; load_observations lines 29-45 iterates EVERY physical archive line and JSON-decodes/constructs each FlowObservation before deque retains only last 100000.

storage.py:72-73 seen-ID skip precedes _semantic_signature comparison at lines 74-78. Thus same-ID metadata-only conflict is not surfaced; first stored version wins for both input permutations across repeated runs.

runner.py:120-121 calls append_observations then load_observations(max_records=100000) again. Therefore even network=False with zero new rows performs two complete archive scans, not a bounded 100000-row read. Approximate work is >=2N row parse operations per run for N stored rows; memory bound does not imply runtime/IO bound.

storage.py:64-83 dedup sees only latest 100000 IDs; replay of an older ID outside this window can be appended. Repeated historical replay can grow N, further increasing every-run scan cost. This is a source-level possibility, not measured production growth.

runner.py:120 has no archive append exception handler; a future fail-closed conflict exception must be reported in audit/health without leaving misleading collector OK or silently losing required output artifacts.

runner.py:121-144 scoring, handoff, evidence_health and three atomic JSON outputs are downstream of append and second scan. evidence_health.py:31-58 collector status is derived from parse attempts/source errors, not archive admission conflicts.
evidence.distinct_from_C: C's normalization equal-rank metadata tie and future-effective PIT filter are downstream; A's first-writer archive conflict and double archive scan occur before normalization and are not solved by C-only normalization changes.
